## Gap, in plain words

The window is Vulkan; the chrome is not. Every pixel of the GUI frame is painted on the CPU and copied into the swapchain.
- GuiFrame::frame paints four lists (Viewport panel, document list, dock, status) with kumihimo-ui's CPU painter into one window-size Canvas (P/hsk-studio-native-host/src/gui/mod.rs:695-705). GuiFrame::upload copies the whole canvas into the pane on every change (:714-723) through Owner::upload_pane, which allocates a new staging buffer per call (P/hsk-studio-vulkan/src/owner.rs:671-680) and records vkCmdCopyBufferToImage (:712-729); the presenter then blits the pane (P/hsk-studio-vulkan/src/present.rs:450-464). At 1920x1080 that is 8 MB per hover change.
- hsk-studio-vulkan has no shader, pipeline or descriptor (src/lib.rs:7-10; DESCRIPTOR :32). The device is created with queues and extensions only, no feature struct (owner.rs:620). A pane has an image and no image view (Pane, owner.rs:413-420), though the image is created with COLOR_ATTACHMENT and SAMPLED usage (:794-799).
- hsk-studio-vulkan depends on ash only (P/hsk-studio-vulkan/Cargo.toml:7-8); root Cargo.toml:315-316 already allows it kumihimo-ui.
- Receipts, the window title, the CLI usage and both descriptors say `cpu painter, Vulkan UI pass pending` (P/hsk-studio-native-host/src/scene.rs:9; window.rs:335, :702; offscreen.rs:106; cli.rs:11; lib.rs:9-10, :36; README.md:3-4, :40-41, :68). A software path never passes a Vulkan obligation (HBR-HOST-001), so no frame of this GUI is Vulkan UI evidence yet (GUI-DESKTOP-020, -024).
- naga 27.0.3 is in Cargo.lock once, through wgpu only (render-gpu Cargo.toml:22 wgpu =27.0.1); its lock entry already lists hexf-parse, spirv and unicode-ident, so wgsl-in and spv-out are compiled today. The quarantine gate names its owners render-gpu, harness and harness-view (handshake-studio-assets/tools/workspace-probe.rs:565-566; tools/ below means that folder), rejects naga in hsk-studio-vulkan's manifest (self-test case :1089) and any .wgsl outside the 9 render-gpu files (TOOLKIT_ALLOWED_WGSL :602-612; tree walk :713-738; gate :741-748). The kumihimo-ui display list, all 11 primitives (P/kumihimo-ui/src/display.rs:32-61, KINDS :81), drawn by the GPU on the host's one device into the existing pane, with a shelf-packed glyph alpha atlas fed from hsk-studio-ui-text's rasters through kumihimo-ui's Text cache and a two-tint icon atlas; offscreen first and pixel-compared against the CPU painter on the spine's frame; then presented in the quiet window behind a host switch `--chrome cpu|vulkan` (new), CPU the default, the CPU painter kept as the reference and the selectable fallback. ## Pixel tolerance and why

- Exact, difference 0: Rect, Edge, Checker, opaque Image, scissor edges, and every pixel the painter wrote at full coverage with an opaque colour. Integer quads put every pixel centre strictly inside or outside, and an opaque source converts back exactly: 'If r is equal to an integer, then that integer value must be returned' (Vulkan fundamentals.adoc, Conversion From Floating-Point to Normalized Fixed-Point). So AC-GEOM-03 shared edges and AC-COL-01 tokens hold bit for bit, as B2 done_when asks (flat colours equal tokens exactly).
- At most 1 per channel per blend: glyphs, icons, translucent Image and Ramp. Coverage is the same integer through the atlas, but blending is 'treated as if carried out in floating-point' at a precision no lower than the destination (framebuffer.adoc), and the float-to-UNORM step returns one of the two closest values and only 'should round to nearest' (fundamentals.adoc), while the painter rounds the exact rational (paint.rs:62-63).
- At most 2 per blend at AA edge pixels of RRect, Line, Dash and Shadow, and 4 where two such blends stack on one pixel (an RRect border then its fill): shader f32 coverage can land on the other side of an 8-bit quantization step, because the backend may contract a product and an add into an FMA (naga emits no NoContraction; measured on this driver as F-R46-1, render-gpu src/kernel.wgsl:361-367), adding one step to the blend's own rounding.
- Every pixel outside the AA rects of a frame (union of glyph, icon, rrect, line, dash, shadow, ramp and translucent image rects, from the trace) is exact. Tests report the max difference and the differing count per class; a class above its bound is red.

## Device loss and swapchain re-creation keep the atlas correct

- The atlas holds no authority: its content is a pure function of (Text epoch, LUT, GlyphKey) and (IconId, px, mask bytes), and pixels never depend on where an entry sits (texel-exact fetch). Any reset, growth or rebuild gives the same frame: a test draws cold, warm, after a reset and after growth and compares bytes.
- Swapchain re-creation (out of date, suboptimal, resize, minimise, surface lost: machine.rs:129-160, present.rs:194-352) does not touch the pass: it draws into the pane and the presenter blits. A pane re-created on resize brings its own view; the next frame draws it.
- Device loss: the pass records the Core (Arc::ptr_eq, as present.rs:375-377) and the owner generation; a mismatch or a poisoned submitter refuses typed; nothing retries; the pass and its atlas go with the owner. A later rebind (generation + 1) builds a new, empty pass, and stale handles never authorize a submit (GUI-DESKTOP-036).
